distillation_scope.leaf_granularity: First-layer disease leaf for placenta previa itself: placental tissue implanted over the internal cervical os. Bleeding severity, placenta accreta spectrum, prior cesarean delivery, gestational age, fetal status, labor, hemodynamic compromise, and delivery-resource context are represented as axes, risk/context modifiers, event hazards, treatment modifiers, or future subtype layers rather than disease-name qualifiers.
distillation_scope.case_source_policy: Distilled without reading real case reports or disease-specific case JSONs for this leaf. Independent case sourcing and audit must remain separate before activation.
distillation_scope.boundary_policy: This leaf is distinct from placental abruption, vasa previa, ectopic pregnancy, miscarriage, cervical/vaginal lesions, uterine rupture, postpartum hemorrhage as a standalone event, and placenta accreta spectrum as an invasive placentation context. When an independent condition is present, use vector-field superposition or context axes without double-counting the same bleeding, shock, fetal, or operative axes.

latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Placental implantation in the lower uterine segment persists into later gestation instead of clearing away from the internal cervical os as the uterus enlarges.
Placental tissue directly overlies the internal cervical os, creating an anatomic barrier to vaginal delivery and a fragile placental edge at the cervix.

Cervical remodeling, lower-segment stretching, uterine activity, or contact shear partially disrupts placental sinuses at the internal os, producing maternal vaginal bleeding that is often painless and bright red.
After a sentinel bleed, repeated bleeding episodes can occur as the lower segment continues to stretch or the cervix changes.
Large or repeated maternal blood loss lowers circulating volume and oxygen delivery, causing tachycardia, falling blood pressure, lactate elevation, shock, and maternal death hazard.
Bleeding recurrence, uterine activity, fetal concern, or maternal instability can force delivery before term, shifting risk toward prematurity-related neonatal complications.
A low placental location can coexist with malpresentation, reduced placental reserve, fetal growth restriction, and nonreassuring fetal status, especially with recurrent bleeding or prematurity.
Low placentation over a uterine scar or abnormal decidualization increases the probability of abnormally adherent or invasive placental tissue, which raises delivery hemorrhage and hysterectomy need.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Greater os overlap makes vaginal delivery less feasible.
More coverage creates a larger placental-cervical interface vulnerable to bleeding.
Contractions or cervical change can shear placental sinuses and increase bleeding.

axis_couplings.conditionality: Weaker before hemodilution or if bleeding is brief and rapidly treated.
axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: More visible bleeding generally lowers maternal hemoglobin.
Severe bleeding sharply increases shock hazard.
Maternal death hazard rises when hemorrhagic shock develops or persists.
Accreta spectrum context increases risk of severe delivery and postpartum hemorrhage.

axis_couplings.conditionality: Strongest when the previa is anterior or overlies the uterine scar.
axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Repeated cesarean scars greatly increase accreta spectrum probability when previa is present.
Higher accreta spectrum suspicion increases complex surgical management need.
Greater gestational age reduces prematurity-related respiratory morbidity hazard.
Nonreassuring fetal status can progress to hypoxic injury if not relieved by delivery or maternal stabilization.
Severe ongoing fetal hypoxia can progress to fetal death.
Digital cervical examination can precipitate severe bleeding when previa is present.

treatments.treatment_name: Planned cesarean delivery for stable placenta previa

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Accreta context increases operative bleeding and resource requirements.
Planned surgery is safer when experienced teams and blood products are available.

treatments.treatment_name: Urgent cesarean delivery for uncontrolled bleeding or fetal compromise

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Active severe bleeding makes source control more urgent.
Delivery can relieve fetal compromise from maternal bleeding or placental dysfunction.
Operative source control is more dangerous without hemorrhage support.

treatments.treatment_name: Expectant monitoring with modified activity and pelvic rest

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Shock requires resuscitation and delivery/source control rather than observation alone.
Fetal compromise changes the treatment vector toward delivery.

treatments.treatment_name: Antenatal corticosteroids for preterm delivery risk

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Steroid benefit depends on gestational age and delivery probability.
Benefit is smaller if delivery is unlikely soon.

treatments.treatment_name: Magnesium sulfate for early preterm neuroprotection context

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Neuroprotection matters when early preterm delivery is likely.
Maternal instability narrows safety margin.

treatments.treatment_name: Maternal hemodynamic resuscitation and massive transfusion activation

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Severe obstetric hemorrhage requires blood products, not crystalloid alone.
Resuscitation alone cannot stop lower-segment or accreta-related bleeding.

treatments.treatment_name: Postpartum hemorrhage prevention and uterotonic support

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Uterotonics do not correct invasive placental adherence.

treatments.treatment_name: Multidisciplinary accreta-context cesarean hysterectomy or complex surgery

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: High accreta context makes planned complex surgery more important.
Complex placenta surgery needs experienced obstetric, anesthesia, blood bank, neonatal, and sometimes urologic/interventional support.

treatments.treatment_name: Short-term tocolysis for stable preterm contractions

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Major bleeding should not be masked by delaying delivery.
Maternal instability requires resuscitation and source control.
Fetal compromise changes the goal toward delivery.

treatments.treatment_name: Rho(D) immune globulin for Rh-negative bleeding context

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Anti-D prophylaxis is relevant to unsensitized Rh-negative patients.

risk_factors.display_name: Prior cesarean delivery or uterine scar

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Prior uterine scar increases previa and accreta context probability.
Previa over a scar markedly raises accreta spectrum concern.

treatment_effect_modulation.multidisciplinary_accreta_context_cesare: relative value increases when scar-related accreta context is high
treatment_effect_modulation.planned_cesarean_delivery_for_stable_pla: requires earlier resource planning and blood-bank preparation

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: The number of prior cesareans modifies scar burden.
Multiple scars increase the chance that complex surgery is needed when previa is present.

present.trajectory_modulation: Raises prior probability of low placental implantation and previa without defining disease subtype.

risk_factors.display_name: Prior uterine curettage, myomectomy, or endometrial injury

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Uterine procedures can alter decidualization and implantation patterns.
Endometrial or myometrial injury increases abnormal adherence context.

risk_factors.display_name: Assisted reproductive technology or multiple gestation

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: ART and multiple gestation increase obstetric complexity and preterm delivery pressure.
Smoking can increase placental dysfunction and fetal growth restriction context.

risk_factors.display_name: Complete os coverage or large overlap

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Complete coverage sharply lowers vaginal delivery feasibility.
Large overlap increases bleeding surface and labor risk.

treatment_effect_modulation.planned_cesarean_delivery_for_stable_pla: delivery source-control value increases as vaginal route feasibility falls

risk_factors.display_name: Active bleeding or hemodynamic compromise context

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Observed active bleeding or compromise raises immediate shock risk.
Maternal compromise increases death hazard until resuscitated and source-controlled.

treatment_effect_modulation.urgent_cesarean_delivery_for_uncontrolle: relative value increases with active severe bleeding or fetal compromise
treatment_effect_modulation.expectant_monitoring_modified_activity_a: standalone role decreases when bleeding or compromise is severe

risk_factors.display_name: Limited blood bank, surgical, anesthesia, or neonatal resources

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Blood product limitation reduces hemorrhage rescue capacity.
Complex previa or accreta context outcomes depend on resource availability.
Resource delay or limitation increases hemorrhage mortality risk.

supportive_care.description: Use ultrasound to define placental relationship to the internal os before digital cervical examination when antepartum bleeding is present.
Track bleeding volume, heart rate, blood pressure, shock index, mental status, urine output, hemoglobin, type and screen, and transfusion needs.
Monitor fetal heart rate, fetal movement, growth, presentation, and nonreassuring tracing according to gestational age and care goals.
Prepare blood products, anesthesia, obstetric surgery, neonatal support, and escalation pathways before bleeding or delivery when feasible.
When prior uterine scar or imaging signs raise accreta context, plan multidisciplinary delivery resources and surgical contingencies.
Follow placental edge-to-os relationship over gestation because low-lying placenta can resolve while true previa may persist.
Check maternal Rh status and provide anti-D prophylaxis when the Rh-negative unsensitized context is present after bleeding.
After delivery, monitor uterine tone, surgical bleeding, hemoglobin, coagulation status, transfusion complications, and recovery from anemia or shock.

quality_notes: Created in staging only; this file should not be moved into active atlas until independent case sourcing, audit, fairness review, and regression pass.

Pure disease-name scope was preserved: bleeding severity, accreta spectrum, prior cesarean delivery, gestational age, fetal status, hemodynamic compromise, and resource state are modeled as axes or modifiers.
The only derived hazard axis is maternal mortality_hazard_in_D-PLACENTA-PREVIA; fetal, bleeding, shock, preterm, neonatal, and alloimmunization risks are event_hazard axes.
Parent/satellite structure is used for pregnancy context, placental location, PAS context, bleeding phenotype, pain, fetal status, malpresentation, hemoglobin change, and Rh context.
Treatment entries are vector-field interventions with context modifiers and failure modes; treatment ordering is intentionally left to forward simulation.
